title: Fix Tcolorbox Height-Bound Image Double-Typeset Bug
description: Root-cause and fix the pre-existing tcolorbox double-typeset/double-paint bug in print/tex/semio-window.sty documented in tickets 26/07/20/INTEGRATE-TEMP-ZWISCHENBERICHT-CONTENT-INTO-MIT-BESTAND-REPORT and 26/07/17/FIX-IMAGE-COVER-ANCHOR-MECHANISM: a height-bound image inside a Figure/Photo/WindowItem (image-fit=contain or cover) either double-renders (ghost/duplicate copy bleeding past crop edge) or produces large constant Overfull \hbox warnings (observed at a fixed 414.84218pt regardless of image size/aspect ratio), whenever a savebox-measured graphic is typeset inside this package's tcolorbox body (enhanced+breakable+nobeforeafter). Reproduces both for standalone height-bound Figure (not in a WindowItem) and WindowItem-wrapped Photo with generous heights. Rebuild print/template/report/report.content.tex's existing Photo/Image/WindowArrangement demo section standalone to check whether it currently reproduces too (confirming pre-existing regression, not appendix-specific), then find the actual tcolorbox/enhanced-box interaction causing the double body typeset (likely related to `breakable` needing a trial-measurement pass when `height=` is set) and fix it at the root in semio-window.sty so Figure/Photo/WindowItem can use proper chrome-styled images at full report size without the workaround of bypassing to plain \includegraphics.
summary:
Extensively investigated the pre-existing tcolorbox height-bound image ghost/overfull bug documented in tickets 26/07/20/INTEGRATE-TEMP-ZWISCHENBERICHT-CONTENT-INTO-MIT-BESTAND-REPORT and 26/07/17/FIX-IMAGE-COVER-ANCHOR-MECHANISM. Confirmed it reproduces standalone via print/template/report/report.content.tex's existing demo section (bun ./script.ts build report), not appendix-specific — visually confirmed via pdftoppm renders and root-caused via raw PDF content-stream inspection (PyMuPDF): each affected Photo emits two separate paint (Do) operators for the same image XObject with an unbalanced graphics-state (q/Q) stack between them, letting a second "ghost" copy paint outside the intended clip region.

Systematically ruled out every angle in our own code as the cause (all changes tested live then reverted, verified via git diff against HEAD after each): box width auto-sizing, breakable vs non-breakable, TikZ bounding-box leakage (useasboundingbox), savebox register reuse, valign/halign positioning, and even collapsing to a single unconditional includegraphics call — the exact same excess persisted through all of them. Decisively confirmed the bug is NOT specific to images or our cover-mode code at all: replacing the image entirely with a bare `\rule` sized to the box's own target dimensions reproduces the same class of overflow. This narrows the root cause to tcolorbox's own internal handling of `height=` + `breakable` + `enhanced` when body content's footprint approaches the box's fixed height — outside what's fixable in semio-window.sty's own macros.

Documented the full reproduction steps, all ruled-out hypotheses, the PDF-level evidence, and suggested next steps (minimal tcolorbox-only repro to confirm/report upstream) in findings.md. No code fix was landed since the root cause sits in tcolorbox itself, not in this package; semio-window.sty and report.content.tex were restored to their exact original state after each experiment (verified via git diff HEAD showing no unintended changes). Also noted for future sessions: an ambient auto-commit process periodically commits the live working tree, which caught one mid-experiment diagnostic edit (a placeholder `\rule` replacing real image rendering) into shared history for a few minutes before it was caught and reverted in a follow-up edit within this same session — worth being aware of when leaving intermediate/broken states in shared files even briefly.
